questions.cardText:
[History] What was the primary motivation for the invention of Hangul?
A. To promote literacy in Korea
B. To distance Korea from Chinese influence
C. To enhance communication with Korea’s neighboring countries
Answer: A. Hangul was scientifically designed to be easy to learn and use. The shapes of the letters are based on the articulatory features of the sounds they represent, making it one of the most logical and efficient writing systems in the world.
questions.de: Was war König Sejongs Hauptbeweggrund für die Erfindung des koreanischen Alphabets Hangeul im 15. Jahrhundert?
questions.en: What was King Sejong's primary motivation for inventing the Korean alphabet Hangul in the 15th century?
questions.answerDe: Die Lese- und Schreibfähigkeit (des einfachen Volkes) zu fördern

timeline.labelEn: King Sejong the Great officially promulgates the Hangul alphabet in the Hunminjeongeum
timeline.labelDe: König Sejong der Große verkündet das Hangeul-Alphabet offiziell im Hunminjeongeum

questions.notes: Wikipedia: Hanja's difficulty contributed to high illiteracy, so Sejong created Hangul; announced 1443/44, promulgated 1446.

questions.cardText:
[Political Science] The concept of a “social contract” is central to the theories of which philosopher?
A. Karl Marx
B. John Locke
C. Thomas Hobbes
Answer: B.
questions.de: Welcher englische Philosoph, Autor der „Zwei Abhandlungen über die Regierung“, gründete legitime Herrschaft auf einen Gesellschaftsvertrag, der Leben, Freiheit und Eigentum der Menschen schützt?
questions.en: Which English philosopher, author of the Two Treatises of Government, based legitimate government on a social contract that protects people's life, liberty and property?

timeline.labelEn: John Locke, English philosopher of the social contract and natural rights
timeline.labelDe: John Locke, englischer Philosoph des Gesellschaftsvertrags und der Naturrechte

questions.notes: Card error: option C (Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan 1651) is equally correct — Hobbes coined the 'state of nature' and is a founding social-contract theorist (as is Rousseau). Reworked with Locke-specific details so only Locke fits.
